name: Feed config into a pod (env & envFrom)
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration & Security. Drill EVERY way to feed config into pods: single-key env, bulk envFrom + prefix, volume mounts with items/subPath, Secrets (env + volume + types), immutable, projected volumes, and a no-hint diagnose-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Single-key env + an optional key
questions.teach:
**Single key → env var:** `env: [{name: X, valueFrom: {configMapKeyRef: {name: cm, key: K}}}]`. Add `optional: true` on a key ref so a **missing** key doesn't block pod start.

**Gotcha:** a referenced key that doesn't exist and isn't `optional` leaves the pod in `CreateContainerConfigError`.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `cfg-env` (`busybox:1.36`, `sh -c 'sleep 3600'`):
- env `MODE` from ConfigMap `app-config` key `APP_MODE`
- env `EXTRA` from `app-config` key `OPTIONAL_KEY`, marked **optional** (that key doesn't exist — the pod must still start)

Target: `MODE` ← app-config/APP_MODE, and `EXTRA` ← app-config/OPTIONAL_KEY with `optional: true`.
questions.hint: `env` with two entries; the second's `configMapKeyRef` needs `optional: true`. Build with `--dry-run=client -o yaml` and edit.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: cfg-env, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: MODE
      valueFrom: { configMapKeyRef: { name: app-config, key: APP_MODE } }
    - name: EXTRA
      valueFrom: { configMapKeyRef: { name: app-config, key: OPTIONAL_KEY, optional: true } }
YAML
questions.eli5:
Imagine your app is a new hire, and a **ConfigMap** is a sticky-note board on the wall with labelled notes on it: `APP_MODE = prod`, and so on. You want to copy certain notes onto the new hire's own name badge (those are **environment variables**) so they always have them handy.

**Single-key env** is you saying: *"Go to the board called `app-config`, read the note labelled `APP_MODE`, and write it on your badge under the name `MODE`."* You pick exactly one note and give it whatever badge-name you like.

Now sometimes you ask for a note that might not be there, like `OPTIONAL_KEY`. If you demand a note that doesn't exist, the new hire freezes at the door and won't start work at all. So you add a little tag that says **optional: true** — meaning *"if that note isn't on the board, no big deal, just skip it and start working."*

That's the whole trick: name the env var, point it at one ConfigMap key, and mark it optional when the key might be missing.

**Watch out for:**

- **A required key that doesn't exist jams the container.** Without `optional: true`, a missing key leaves the pod stuck in **CreateContainerConfigError** — it never starts.
- **`optional: true` goes inside the key reference**, right next to `name` and `key` — not on the env var itself.
- **The env var name and the key name are separate things.** `MODE` is the badge name; `APP_MODE` is the note on the board. They don't have to match.
- **The ConfigMap must be in the same namespace** as the pod — a pod can't read a board from another room.
questions.deepDive:
## Single-key env from a ConfigMap — full rundown

### Mental model
A ConfigMap is a bag of `key: value` strings. **`env` + `valueFrom.configMapKeyRef`** copies **one** key into **one** environment variable inside the container. You choose the env var's name independently of the key's name. The value is read **once, at container start** — editing the ConfigMap later does *not* update an already-running container's env.

### The manifest
```yaml
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: MODE                       # env var name (your choice)
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: app-config             # the ConfigMap
          key: APP_MODE                # the key inside it
    - name: EXTRA
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: app-config
          key: OPTIONAL_KEY
          optional: true               # missing key → skip, pod still starts
```

### env vs envFrom
| | `env` + `valueFrom.configMapKeyRef` | `envFrom` + `configMapRef` |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | one specific key | every key in the ConfigMap |
| Rename | yes — you set the env var name | no — key name becomes the env var name |
| Prefix | n/a | optional `prefix:` |
| Best for | picking/renaming a few values | bulk injection |

### `valueFrom` sources you can use
| `valueFrom.*` | Reads from |
|---|---|
| `configMapKeyRef` | one ConfigMap key |
| `secretKeyRef` | one Secret key |
| `fieldRef` | pod metadata (Downward API) |
| `resourceFieldRef` | container resource request/limit |

### The `optional` flag
- `optional: true` on a `configMapKeyRef`/`secretKeyRef` → a **missing key, or a missing ConfigMap/Secret entirely**, is tolerated: that env var is simply not set and the pod starts normally.
- `optional: false` (the **default**) → a missing key or object blocks container creation.

### Imperative scaffold
```bash
# generate a pod skeleton, then hand-edit the env block
kubectl -n ckad-config run cfg-env --image=busybox:1.36 \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml --command -- sh -c 'sleep 3600' > p.yaml
# add the env: block shown above, then:
kubectl apply -f p.yaml
```
```bash
# inspect what the container actually got
kubectl -n ckad-config exec cfg-env -- env | grep -E 'MODE|EXTRA'
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Required missing key ⇒ `CreateContainerConfigError`.** `kubectl describe pod` Events: *"couldn't find key APP_MODE in ConfigMap app-config"*. Fix the ConfigMap (add the key) or mark the ref `optional`.
- **`optional: true` belongs inside `configMapKeyRef`/`secretKeyRef`**, not at the `env` entry level.
- **Env is a point-in-time snapshot.** Unlike a mounted ConfigMap volume, env vars do **not** auto-refresh when the ConfigMap changes; restart the pod to pick up new values.
- **Namespace-scoped.** The ConfigMap must live in the pod's namespace.
- **Names are independent.** `name:` under `env` is the variable; `key:` is the ConfigMap key. Don't conflate them.
- All ConfigMap values are **strings** — numbers/booleans arrive as text.

### Quick reference
```yaml
env:
- name: MODE
  valueFrom: { configMapKeyRef: { name: app-config, key: APP_MODE } }
- name: EXTRA
  valueFrom: { configMapKeyRef: { name: app-config, key: OPTIONAL_KEY, optional: true } }
```
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-config exec cfg-env -- env    # verify MODE set, EXTRA absent
```

questions.title: Bulk envFrom with a prefix
questions.teach:
**Bulk → env:** `envFrom: [{configMapRef: {name: cm}}]` injects **every** key as an env var. Add `prefix: CFG_` to namespace them all (`CFG_APP_MODE`…).

**Gotcha:** `envFrom` can't rename individual keys — for that use single-key `valueFrom` instead.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `cfg-envfrom` (`busybox:1.36`, sleep) that bulk-injects **all** keys of ConfigMap `app-config` as env vars with prefix `CFG_`.

Target: `envFrom` references configMapRef `app-config` with `prefix: CFG_`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: cfg-envfrom, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    envFrom:
    - prefix: CFG_
      configMapRef: { name: app-config }
YAML

verification.description: cfg-envfrom: envFrom app-config with prefix CFG_

questions.eli5:
Last time you copied **one** note from the sticky-note board onto the new hire's badge. **envFrom** is the lazy, bulk version: *"take the WHOLE board called `app-config` and copy every single note onto the badge automatically."* Ten notes on the board? You get ten badge entries, each keeping its original label.

Because dumping a big pile of notes onto a badge can get confusing (what if two boards both have a note called `MODE`?), you can add a **prefix** — like stamping `CFG_` on the front of every copied note. So `APP_MODE` becomes `CFG_APP_MODE`, `COLOR` becomes `CFG_COLOR`, and so on. Now you can tell at a glance which notes came from which board, and two boards won't clash.

The trade-off: with envFrom you take **all or nothing**, and you **can't rename individual notes**. If you only want one note, or you want to call it something totally different, you go back to the one-note-at-a-time method (`valueFrom`).

**Watch out for:**

- **envFrom can't rename or pick individual keys** — it's bulk, whole-ConfigMap. For renaming a single value, use single-key `valueFrom` instead.
- **The prefix applies to the whole source**, stamped on every key. It goes on the `envFrom` entry, not on the ConfigMap.
- **Keys that aren't valid env var names get silently skipped** (e.g. a key with a dash like `my-key`), and an event is logged — they won't appear.
- **If the referenced ConfigMap is missing** and not marked `optional`, the pod won't start.
- **Env is a snapshot at start-up** — later edits to the board don't update a running container.
questions.deepDive:
## Bulk env with envFrom + prefix — full rundown

### Mental model
`envFrom` injects **every** key of a ConfigMap (or Secret) as an environment variable in one shot. Each ConfigMap key becomes an env var of the **same name** (optionally with a prefix). It's the bulk counterpart to single-key `env`/`valueFrom`.

### The manifest
```yaml
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    envFrom:
    - prefix: CFG_                    # stamped onto every key (optional)
      configMapRef:
        name: app-config
    # - secretRef: { name: app-secret }   # same idea for Secrets
```
A ConfigMap key `APP_MODE=prod` becomes env var `CFG_APP_MODE=prod`.

### `envFrom` entry fields
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `configMapRef.name` | pull all keys from this ConfigMap |
| `secretRef.name` | pull all keys from this Secret |
| `prefix` | string prepended to **every** resulting env var name |
| `optional` | if `true`, a missing ConfigMap/Secret is tolerated |

### envFrom vs env — when to use which
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| All keys, keep their names | `envFrom` |
| All keys, namespaced | `envFrom` + `prefix` |
| One/few keys | `env` + `valueFrom.configMapKeyRef` |
| Rename a key | `env` + `valueFrom` (envFrom **can't** rename) |
| Mark one key optional | `env` + `valueFrom … optional: true` |

### Invalid key names
ConfigMap keys that aren't valid C-identifier env var names (e.g. contain `-`, `.`, or start with a digit) are **skipped**, and the kubelet records an event. With a `prefix`, the prefix+key must still form a valid name.

### Precedence rules
- If multiple `envFrom` sources define the same variable, **later entries win**.
- An explicit `env:` entry with the same name as an `envFrom`-derived one **overrides** the `envFrom` value (explicit `env` has highest precedence).

### Imperative scaffold
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-config run cfg-envfrom --image=busybox:1.36 \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml --command -- sh -c 'sleep 3600' > p.yaml
# add the envFrom block, then apply
kubectl apply -f p.yaml
kubectl -n ckad-config exec cfg-envfrom -- env | grep CFG_
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **No per-key rename or selection.** `envFrom` is all-or-nothing on a source; for one renamed key use `env`/`valueFrom`.
- **`prefix` is per-source**, on the `envFrom` list entry — it applies to every key from that source.
- **Invalid-named keys silently dropped** (dash/dot/leading digit) — don't rely on them appearing.
- **Missing source blocks start** unless `optional: true` on that `configMapRef`/`secretRef`.
- **Env is a start-time snapshot** — ConfigMap edits don't propagate to running containers (mounted volumes do, env doesn't).
- Works identically for Secrets via `secretRef` — values are base64-decoded into the env vars.

### Quick reference
```yaml
envFrom:
- prefix: CFG_
  configMapRef: { name: app-config }
```
```bash
kubectl -n ckad-config exec cfg-envfrom -- env | grep CFG_   # CFG_APP_MODE=...
```
